channel.title: Recent Updates on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Recent Updates on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 31
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s latest weekly release adds more model choice and content protection controls. VS Code also gets new options for managing agent sessions and preparing pull requests for merge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GPT-6 Astra is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the model is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: KubeletInUserNamespace (aka Rootless mode) Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 moves KubeletInUserNamespace to beta and enables the feature gate by default. It allows node components to run as a non-root user in a Linux user namespace, reducing host impact from node-component exploits, while leaving existing rootful clusters unchanged unless explicitly configured.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: New API endpoint provides privacy-safe star history data
item.description:
GitHub added a new REST API endpoint for repository star history that lets users track star growth over time without exposing individual stargazer identities. This follows earlier restrictions on stargazer listing endpoints to admins and collaborators.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
item.description:
GitHub says three npm publishing updates are now generally available, including support for multiple trusted publishing configurations per package. The post also mentions staged publishing and another publishing-related change, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Early September 2026 updates
item.description:
GitHub Actions added three updates focused on workflow visibility and control. The post highlights a new REST API for runner version deprecations, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details of the other changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The affected models include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI Linux package signing key expires September 5
item.description:
The GitHub CLI Linux package repository signing key expires on September 5, 2026. After that date, repository metadata in APT and RPM workflows will be affected starting with the first release published after expiration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.8 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed strong performance on complex terminal-based coding tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: DRA Updates
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 adds several DRA updates, including GA support for extended resources, stable device taints/tolerations, and stable standardized NUMA node attributes. It also promotes multiple DRA features to Beta or Alpha, with focus areas including workload-level ResourceClaims, device metadata/status, scheduling performance, and fractional consumable capacity.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: dotnet: Test what you ship: MSTest and Native AOT
item.description:
MSTest source generation now lets test projects run with the same Native AOT and trimming deployment model as the apps they validate. It also reduces reflection on the test execution path.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager IPAM in additional Azure regions
item.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management is now generally available in additional regions: US Gov Virginia, US Gov Texas, US Gov Arizona, China North 3, and China East 3.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft says Unicode-based “ASCII smuggling,” previously used to hide instructions from AI models, is now being used to obfuscate email content before filters parse it, enabling phishing evasion.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Reopening Copilot Business and Enterprise signups
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise for customers paying by credit card or PayPal over the next few weeks. Availability is rolling out gradually to people who have been waiting to start.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.4 improves GitHub actions security detections
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.4 is a new release that adds support for Go 1.27 and improves GitHub Actions security detections. It is part of the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes a human-operated campaign that uses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support, obtain remote access, and deploy a Node.js-based implant. The post also explains how attackers use legitimate tools for lateral movement and how Microsoft Defender can help detect and disrupt the activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings can now set any supported GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations. This lets enterprises choose the default model that best matches their workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HorizontalPodAutoscaler
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale workloads down to zero replicas by default when using object or external metrics. The feature is Beta; it requires a metric source that remains available at zero replicas, and the controller marks zero-state ownership with a ScaledToZero condition.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusion policies set at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. Excluded files will not be used as context by Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
item.description:
Azure Front Door Web Application Firewall (WAF) now supports associating WAF policies at the profile and route levels in public preview. This lets you apply baseline protection across a profile and more targeted policies on specific routes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Reader Endpoint for Azure Database for MySQL
item.description:
Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server now has a public preview of a reader endpoint to simplify connection management when using multiple replicas. The endpoint provides automatic load balancing for read-only connections.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise: Tracking a deceptive software download campaign
item.description:
Microsoft describes an active malware campaign that impersonates legitimate software vendors using look-alike download pages and regenerated installer archives. The post includes observed techniques, Defender XDR detections, indicators of compromise, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)
item.description:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud now supports Azure Container Apps environments in its Serverless Containers Posture experience. This lets security teams manage posture for more of their container estate from one workflow.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Windows Server 2025 on AKS
item.description:
AKS now supports Windows Server 2025 in general availability, giving customers a newer Windows node option for Windows-based Kubernetes workloads on Azure. This is intended to help with modernization as older Windows Server versions near retirement.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Artifact Streaming on AKS
item.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now supports Artifact streaming with Azure Container Registry (ACR) in generally available form. It is intended to reduce wait time when starting containerized workloads by allowing images to be used before they are fully pulled.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Confidential VMs for Azure Linux
item.description:
Confidential Virtual Machines for Azure Linux in AKS are now generally available. This adds CVM node pool support for migrating highly sensitive container workloads to AKS.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise Live Migrations from GHES to ghe.com generally available
item.description:
Enterprise Live Migrations is now generally available for near-zero-downtime repository migrations from GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency (GHEC DR).

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set an expiration date for individual user budgets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you set an optional expiration date on an individual user budget. When the date is reached, GitHub automatically removes the budget; the feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
item.description:
Copilot code review can now indicate when a pull request is ready for approval, and repository admins can authorize it to approve the PR. The approval capability is disabled by default.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Cybersecurity IR Workshop: The workshop you shouldn’t miss
item.description:
Microsoft Security promoted a cybersecurity incident response workshop focused on practical guidance from DART to improve preparedness and response. The post frames resilience as starting before an incident.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Purchase order mapping available in Microsoft Marketplace
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace purchase order mapping is now generally available. It lets organizations allocate Microsoft invoices, including Marketplace purchases, to support accounting and reconciliation of cloud and AI spend.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: etcd RangeStream Cuts Memory Use on Large List Reads
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates the EtcdRangeStream feature to beta and enables it by default. With etcd v3.7+, the API server can stream large collection reads instead of assembling whole pages in memory, reducing peak memory use and making it more predictable.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes
item.description:
Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes is now generally available. It periodically learns registered and private destination prefixes and applies them as No-SNAT ranges to preserve original source IPs and reduce manual SNAT management.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Copilot Observability Agent supports Basic and Auxiliary table plans
item.description:
Azure Copilot Observability Agent now supports Log Analytics data stored in Basic and Auxiliary table plans for interactive analysis and deep investigations. This extends coverage to high-volume telemetry in Azure Monitor.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Block users from discussion comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub added in-context blocking controls for discussion comments in repositories owned by personal accounts. Users can now block or unblock other users directly from discussion comments, matching the existing issue and pull request comment behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan in Azure Government and China regions
item.description:
Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan is now generally available in Azure Government (Fairfax) and China regions. The plan is intended for cost-effective ingestion and retention of high-volume, verbose logs for compliance and auditing.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan support for Azure tables and plan switching
item.description:
Azure Monitor Logs Auxiliary table plan now supports Azure tables and switching plans, and both capabilities are generally available. The plan is intended for high-volume, low-query logs used for compliance and auditing.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 from Anthropic is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI: Media in issues, pull requests, and comments
item.description:
GitHub CLI now supports a repeatable --attach flag to upload local images or videos and insert them inline in issue, pull request, or comment bodies. This adds media attachment support to GitHub CLI posts and comments.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Per-disk resiliency for Azure VMs
item.description:
Azure VMs now have a public preview option for per-disk resiliency. By default, Azure still recovers a VM by shutting it down and powering it back on after managed disk connectivity is restored.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot model access update for GitHub Team plans
item.description:
GitHub updated how Copilot model access is determined for users with seats in more than one organization. The change is intended to keep billing and governance aligned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected GitHub Copilot models deprecated
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated selected Copilot models across most Copilot experiences, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions, effective September 1, 2026. The post notes that the affected models are no longer available in those experiences.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: AppNet 2026-08-19
item.description:
AppNet 2026-08-19 adds public preview availability in more Azure regions, retires AppNet 1.0–1.2, and updates supported versions to Istio 1.28.10, 1.29.6, and new AppNet 1.5 on Istio 1.30.3. The release also includes fixes for cluster validation, gateway CRD conflicts, certificate rotation, multicluster traffic, identity-based updates, cleanup on delete/leave, diagnostics, and clearer error reporting.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Multicloud Interconnect
item.description:
Azure Multicloud Interconnect is now in public preview. It provides managed private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers, with AWS as the first provider available in preview.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Storage Version Migration Enabled by Default
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes built-in StorageVersionMigration (storagemigration.k8s.io/v1) GA and enabled by default in all clusters. It lets administrators and CRD authors declaratively rewrite stored objects to the current storage version, replacing manual re-write scripts or the out-of-tree migrator.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: commandline: Designing product simplicity for the AI era
item.description:
The article asks whether shared design components are sufficient for a seamless product experience, or whether designers need to prioritize simplicity over complexity to create consistency. It frames this as a product design question for the AI era.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, August 2026 releases
item.description:
VS Code v1.132 through v1.135, released in August 2026, add improvements to GitHub Copilot workflows focused on organizing agent sessions, reviewing changes, and navigating longer conversations. The changelog also mentions updates to Agent Host, but the provided excerpt does not include the details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: TerminalFix campaign deploys a reverse tunnel through multistage intrusion
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed the TerminalFix ClickFix campaign, which uses fake CAPTCHA prompts, DLL sideloading, and a reverse tunnel in a multistage intrusion. The post includes detections and hunting guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Workload identity support for Azure Files CSI driver (SMB) in Azure
item.description:
Azure Files CSI driver for AKS now supports workload identity for pod-level authentication to SMB file shares. This adds an alternative to managed identity for accessing Azure Files from pods.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — August update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s August 2026 update adds more control over Copilot reasoning, model selection, sharing specialized agents within teams, and timing code review requests. The post is a high-level changelog summary rather than a detailed feature list.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 24
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 24 weekly release notes highlight more control over Copilot behavior across Slack, Teams, the app, CLI, and IDEs. The post mentions team sessions in Slack and Teams plus broader customization options, but the provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 graduates Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles to GA, adding built-in support for workload X.509 identity and trust bundle distribution. The feature uses Kubelet, PodCertificateRequest objects, and signer controllers to issue and rotate certificates for TLS/mTLS while keeping key material on the node filesystem.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure VM Image Builder in sovereign and air-gapped clouds
item.description:
Azure VM Image Builder is now generally available in Azure Government, China North 3, Azure Government Secret, and Azure Government Top Secret. The service can be used across these sovereign and air-gapped environments with the same managed image-building experience.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
item.description:
GitHub says three upcoming changes are coming to Copilot policies and billing. The post is a notice to review the updates, but the provided excerpt does not include the actual policy or billing details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Better label management on issues is generally available
item.description:
GitHub says improved label management for issues is now generally available. The update is aimed at making labels easier to organize and find in repositories with large or growing label lists.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Resolution reasons and expanded capabilities
item.description:
Copilot code review now supports two additional pull request types: PRs authored by bots (including Copilot cloud agent) and very large pull requests. GitHub also added resolution reasons for code review outcomes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Classroom deprecated
item.description:
GitHub Classroom was deprecated on August 28, 2026 and replaced by selected partner solutions. The Classroom website, APIs, and related services have been decommissioned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention will cover checks, workflow runs, and statuses
item.description:
Starting October 1, 2026, GitHub Actions retention settings will also apply to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, in addition to artifacts and logs. These data types will follow the same retention policy going forward.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Metrics API graduates to stable
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates the Metrics API from v1beta1 to stable v1. The API surface is unchanged, and v1beta1 remains available for compatibility.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: commandline: Your agent’s guardrails have a bypass
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Agent Hooks, an open, framework-neutral governance contract for agent systems. It includes conformance testing and is intended to make enforcement fail closed instead of failing open when controls crash.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: How Uno Platform uses .NET, MCP, and AI to build high quality apps
item.description:
Uno Platform built two MCP servers in C# to let AI agents use real documentation as context and interact with a running cross-platform .NET app. The post describes how .NET, MCP, and AI are combined to support app development and validation.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Close all open contributions authored by a blocked user
item.description:
GitHub added an option to automatically close all open issues, discussions, and pull requests from a user when you block them from a personal account or organization. This applies to contributions authored by the blocked user at the time the block is set.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: August 2026
item.description:
August 2026 Microsoft Security updates add capabilities for monitoring agent activity, broaden security coverage across supported environments, and improve security management across environments. The post is a high-level roundup and does not list specific product changes in the provided excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support autoUpdate for plugin marketplaces
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings now let admins enable automatic updates for specific plugin marketplaces by setting autoUpdate: true on an extraKnownMarketplaces entry. Supported clients will check the marketplace and update it automatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Global model policy generally available
item.description:
GitHub is gradually rolling out enforcement of a default global model policy for generally available GitHub Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. The policy was announced in July and is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Bastion shareable link expiration
item.description:
Azure Bastion shareable links now support an administrator-defined expiration date and time. After expiration, the link can no longer be used to connect.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: IPv6 dual-stack support for Azure Bastion
item.description:
Azure Bastion now supports IPv4 and IPv6 dual-stack configurations in public preview. New Bastion deployments can be configured with both IPv4 and IPv6 public IP addresses.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Connect to AKS clusters using Azure Bastion
item.description:
Azure Bastion integration with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available. It lets customers create a secure tunnel from a local machine through Azure Bastion to an AKS cluster API server.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Introducing Live Reports for Azure SRE Agent
item.description:
Live Reports are now in Public Preview for Azure SRE Agent. They let operations teams create dynamic operational views from SRE Agent conversations and keep them updated with the latest data.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SRE Agent VNet Integration
item.description:
Azure SRE Agent VNet Integration is now generally available. It lets the agent operate within existing network controls such as NSGs, private DNS, and firewall policies.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SRE Agent 30-Day Trial
item.description:
Azure SRE Agent is now generally available with a 30-day trial for new customers. The trial lets users create agents, connect operational tools and data sources, and evaluate the product at their own pace.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: When AI infrastructure becomes the target: Securing gateways and control points
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports on attacks against exposed AI infrastructure, focusing on LiteLLM gateway exploitation and related credential theft, persistence, and cryptomining activity. The post highlights gateways and other control points as targets that need protection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Apps can now access enterprise billing data
item.description:
GitHub Apps can now be granted access to enterprise billing data by enterprise owners. The app configuration flow now includes an enterprise billing permission that can be selected when creating or updating an app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Garhwal
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 ships 67 enhancements: 16 Stable, 23 Beta, 27 Alpha, and 1 deprecation/removal. Key changes include resilient watchcache initialization, HPA scale-to-zero, manifest-based admission config, Pod checkpoint/restore, broader Dynamic Resource Allocation support, and multiple scheduler, storage, node, and observability updates.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Rule insights dashboard generally available
item.description:
The rule insights dashboard is now generally available for both repositories and organizations. It provides a visual, high-level view of how GitHub evaluates and enforces repository rules.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app Customize tab is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s new Customize tab in the Copilot app is now generally available. It is meant to connect Copilot with a team’s existing tools, knowledge, and workflows, including MCP.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Aspire 13.5 has shipped
item.description:
Aspire 13.5 has shipped. This release refreshes the dashboard and aspire.dev, expands the Interaction Service, adds cross-scope Azure references and persistent Kubernetes volumes, and introduces live terminals in the apphost.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Block users directly from security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository owners block a user directly from a security advisory page in public repositories. The feature is available for repositories owned by organizations or personal accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure 248 and 372 vCPU sizes for D/E v7 series VMs
item.description:
Azure has generally available 248- and 372-vCPU D/E v7 VM sizes in the Dlsv7, Dsv7, Elsv7, and Esv7 families, powered by Intel Xeon 6 processors. Microsoft says these sizes provide up to 20% better compute performance than prior Intel-based v6 VMs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Push rules in rulesets now support path exceptions
item.description:
Push rules in GitHub rulesets now support path exceptions, letting you exempt specific file paths so a rule applies everywhere else in scope. The feature is available in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: .NET Conf 2026
item.description:
.NET Conf 2026 is scheduled for November 10-12, 2026. The event will include three days of sessions and community content and will coincide with the launch of .NET 11.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: The patch window is collapsing: Why security needs a new control plane
item.description:
Microsoft Security says organizations need protection that works between vulnerability discovery and remediation, because the patch window is shrinking. The post argues for a new security control plane to cover that gap.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: One requirement, many failure paths: Evaluate, control, and optimize with ASSERT and ACS
item.description:
The article says a safety requirement can have a complex runtime failure surface even when it seems simple. It highlights ASSERT for finding coverage bugs and ACS for fixing the policy.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: Announcing: Extended Support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now offers Extended Support to keep workloads on supported PostgreSQL versions while you transition to newer releases. It includes critical security updates, critical bug fixes, and technical support.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: From dotnet run to Foundry Hosted Agent in 3 lines of C#
item.description:
Microsoft says an agent built with Microsoft Agent Framework can be deployed to Foundry Hosted Agent with 1 NuGet package, 3 lines of C#, and 2 commands.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS
item.description:
eBPF Host Routing for Advanced Container Networking Services in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available. It moves packet forwarding and routing decisions into the Linux kernel to improve Kubernetes networking performance.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node 22 LTS ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node 22 LTS on Azure App Service ends April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running after that date, but security updates and customer support for Node 22 LTS will stop.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Custom block response code and body for Application Gateway WAF
item.description:
Azure WAF on Application Gateway is now generally available with support for custom block response status codes and response bodies for blocked requests. This lets you define the HTTP response returned when WAF blocks a request.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Explore new features available in C# 15 preview
item.description:
C# 15, shipping with .NET 11, adds union types, closed hierarchies, a preview of the updated unsafe model, and several smaller changes that reduce everyday boilerplate.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Better tools for managing blocked users
item.description:
GitHub updated blocked-user management for personal accounts and organizations. The blocked users list now supports search, sorting, and pagination to make large lists easier to manage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: The new GitHub Copilot experience in Slack
item.description:
GitHub’s Slack integration now includes agentic GitHub Copilot capabilities from Copilot CLI and the Copilot app, available in public preview. Users can interact with @GitHub in Slack to work with these features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Shared agentic work with GitHub Copilot in Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now be started from Microsoft Teams by mentioning @GitHub in a channel, thread, or direct message. This creates a shared agent session that participants can view and help guide.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Stop restricting the agent. Start restricting its environment.
item.description:
Azure SRE Agent argues that AI safety is better achieved by constraining the runtime environment rather than the agent itself. This approach aims to preserve autonomy while reducing risk compared with human review or standing credentials.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Pinning saved views to the repository issues sidebar is generally available and more
item.description:
GitHub now lets you pin saved views to a repository’s issues sidebar, so frequently used views are easier to access. The feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Windows 11 arm64 VS2026 image generally available
item.description:
Windows 11 arm64 images with Visual Studio 2026 are now generally available on standard and larger GitHub-hosted runners. Workflows can use the new image by updating the runner image reference.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement
item.description:
Azure Gateway now generally supports advertising summarized (aggregated) prefixes to on-premises networks instead of advertising every individual virtual network prefix. This is available for route advertisement in Azure gateways.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Copilot introduces direct access to agents
item.description:
Starting in August 2026, Azure Copilot will let customers interact directly with agents to move from questions to actions faster. Users can choose the agent best suited to their goal.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code scanning adds a mitigated alert dismissal reason
item.description:
Code scanning now supports dismissing alerts with the reason “Mitigated” when the vulnerability still exists in code but is offset by external controls, such as a web application firewall or network protections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Separate GitHub Actions path for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality CodeQL Actions workflows now have a dedicated workflow path and are generally available. Run history and Actions usage reports can now distinguish GitHub Code Quality runs from other Actions workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track GitHub Code Quality enablement changes in the audit log
item.description:

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Open source license compliance is in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has put open source license compliance into public preview for enterprises. The feature adds centralized, ruleset-based checks to enforce dependency license policy and block noncompliant licenses.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s June 2026 security update post says the month’s changes focus on identity and multicloud foundations, data protection across locations, and securing developer workflows for AI-related work. The provided excerpt does not include product-level details or specific feature announcements.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
item.description:
The post explains MCP tool poisoning as an attack that can turn trusted AI agents into a control plane for data loss. It describes how attackers manipulate tool descriptions to induce unauthorized actions, and outlines detection, containment, and prevention approaches.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Dependabot no longer infers .npmrc
item.description:
Dependabot no longer infers .npmrc settings for npm private registries. Instead of reconstructing .npmrc from lockfile URLs, it will stop trying to guess configuration based on potentially incorrect lockfile data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming cloud data retention policy for closed security alerts
item.description:
GitHub will begin enforcing a cloud data retention policy for closed Dependabot security alerts on August 25, 2026. The post says this provides a defined retention period for alert data, but it does not include the exact duration in the excerpt provided.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Per-user AI credit budgets available for cost centers
item.description:
Enterprise admins can now assign a per-user AI credit budget to a cost center, with the budget applying to each individual member. The budget updates as cost center membership changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: .NET 8 and .NET 9 will reach End of Support on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says .NET 8 and .NET 9 will both reach end of support on November 10, 2026. The post directs users to upgrade to .NET 10, which is the next LTS release.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: SkiaSharp 4.0 is here: announcing the first stable release
item.description:
SkiaSharp 4.148.0 is the first stable release of SkiaSharp v4. The post says it covers what’s new in this release and references a live event on June 30.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Packaging and Package Identity for .NET apps with WinApp CLI on Windows
item.description:
Microsoft describes using the WinApp CLI to add package identity and create packages for .NET desktop apps on Windows. This enables deeper Windows integration and simpler distribution.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) is now in preview for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Claude Opus 4.8 in preview with fast mode enabled. GitHub says fast mode increases output token speed while keeping the same model intelligence.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Chromium extension uses AI‑related branding to redirect browser search
item.description:
Microsoft reports a malicious Chromium extension that used AI-related branding to impersonate Perplexity AI and redirect browser search traffic. The extension relied on MV3 APIs and intermediary infrastructure to steer searches away from intended destinations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Restrict issue creation to collaborators only
item.description:
Repository admins can now limit issue creation to collaborators with write access. This adds control over who can open issues and helps reduce unwanted issue creation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track total merges by adoption phase in enterprise and organization reports
item.description:
GitHub enterprise and organization reports now include the total number of pull requests merged by each AI adoption phase cohort. This extends the adoption phase metrics previously added to the Copilot usage metrics API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Read-only Actions cache for untrusted triggers
item.description:
GitHub Actions now uses read-only cache tokens on the default branch for workflow events that can be triggered without repository write permissions. This narrows cache access for untrusted triggers by applying least privilege.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Open source maintainership in the age of AI
item.description:
Kubernetes says AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but maintainers must keep human accountability, transparency, and verification at the center. The community is also testing AI review tools such as Copilot and CodeRabbit to help with pull request review and maintainer workload.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1-Flash for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise
item.description:
MAI-Code-1-Flash, Microsoft AI’s in-house coding model, is now generally available for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise. It builds on its recent expansion across Copilot surfaces and is described as purpose-built for coding and optimized.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Desktop 3.6: Worktrees and deeper Copilot integration
item.description:
GitHub Desktop 3.6 adds Git worktree support and expands GitHub Copilot integration for commit authoring and merge conflict resolution. It brings more of the Git workflow into Desktop.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release - 2026-06-19
item.description:
AKS 2026-06-19 adds Kubernetes 1.36 GA/LTS, Application Gateway for Containers GA, and several platform updates including FIPS on Ubuntu 22.04, CVM with Azure Linux GA, and multiple CSI/CNI/component patch upgrades. It also changes some defaults and validations, including Istio CNI behavior for new asm-1-30 installs, dual-stack IPv6 CIDR derivation, and stricter checks for gMSA and FIPS/Kata combinations.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: security: Photo ZIP campaign targeting hospitality industry delivers Node.js implant for persistent access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported an active multi-stage intrusion campaign targeting hospitality organizations in Europe and Asia. The attackers use photo-themed ZIP archives and fake image shortcut files to deploy a persistent Node.js implant and avoid detection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: k8s: Introducing the Cluster API plugin for Headlamp
item.description:
Headlamp now has an alpha Cluster API plugin that adds visual management and debugging views for CAPI resources inside the UI. It covers cluster health, resource hierarchies, scaling, bootstrap config inspection, topology awareness, map view, and inline Prometheus metrics support.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Analysis depth and efficiency updates
item.description:
Copilot code review now uses built-in file exploration tools from the Copilot CLI and SDK. GitHub says this improves review cost efficiency without changing the existing workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support strictKnownMarketplaces in VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed support for strictKnownMarketplaces in VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI. The setting is in public preview and lets enterprises control which plugins users can install.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Inspect Volcano workloads faster with Headlamp
item.description:
The Volcano plugin for Headlamp adds dedicated views for Volcano Jobs, Queues, and PodGroups, plus a map view that shows how they relate to Pods and events. It is meant to improve interactive troubleshooting and inspection of batch workloads without replacing kubectl or the Volcano CLI.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Saved views for repository issues – Public Preview and adjustable row heights in projects
item.description:
GitHub added saved views to repository Issues pages in public preview, allowing teams to create and share filtered issue views. The release also includes adjustable row heights in Projects.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: More control over your GitHub-hosted runners
item.description:
GitHub Actions org admins can now control access to GitHub-hosted runners more tightly. They can disable standard hosted-runner labels like ubuntu-latest and add custom labels for finer-grained usage control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: See your serverless: introducing the Headlamp plugin for Knative
item.description:
Headlamp now has a Knative plugin that adds integrated views and actions for Knative resources in the Kubernetes UI. It centralizes KService management, traffic splitting, autoscaling configuration, metrics, and related CRDs, with release 0.3.0-beta available.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Actions steps can now be run in parallel
item.description:
GitHub Actions now supports running workflow steps concurrently by running them in the background. Previously, steps always executed sequentially, with each step waiting for the prior one to finish.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm adds preventive account protection for high-impact accounts
item.description:
npm now applies a temporary preventive safeguard to high-impact accounts when it detects sensitive account changes. The measure is intended to reduce account-takeover risk for maintainers of widely used packages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Migrate from Azure Blueprints by January 31, 2027
item.description:
Azure Blueprints retirement has been extended from July 11, 2026 to January 31, 2027. Phased retirement starts July 31, 2026, when creating new blueprint definitions will no longer be supported.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Microsoft a Leader in The Forrester Wave™ for Endpoint Management Platforms
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in Forrester Wave: Endpoint Management Platforms, Q2 2026, and reports the highest scores in the current offering and strategy categories.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Red Hat Enterprise Linux runner images are now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub-hosted larger runners now support Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 images in public preview. The images were introduced in partnership with Red Hat and are available for organizations to use.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available after a public preview that began in March 2026. GitHub says it has added several improvements since preview, including model selection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Cost centers now support enterprise teams
item.description:
GitHub cost centers now support adding enterprise teams as resources, so usage can be attributed according to your team structure. This update extends cost attribution for enterprises beyond individual resources.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers – Inference gateway
item.description:
Application Gateway for Containers is adding a preview inference gateway capability. It brings the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension to support AI inference traffic handling for Kubernetes workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on WG Device Management
item.description:
The Device Management WG is working on Kubernetes support for GPUs, TPUs, NICs, and other specialized hardware through Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), which graduated to GA in Kubernetes 1.34. The group is now expanding DRA and related APIs for sharing, topology-aware scheduling, health monitoring, and multi-node device use.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: security: CNAPP evolution: How Microsoft aligns with leading cloud risk management platforms
item.description:
Microsoft’s post says CNAPP platforms are increasingly used to prioritize exploitable risks, reduce exposure, and embed security across the application lifecycle. It positions Microsoft’s approach as aligned with other leading cloud risk management platforms.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Self-service credential revocation for incident response
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise owners can now use a new break-glass capability to immediately revoke all credentials for a compromised account or stolen credentials during incident response. The feature is self-service and intended for urgent security handling.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: StealC and Amadey: Breaking down infostealers and the cybercrime services that deliver them
item.description:
Microsoft’s DCU helped disrupt domains supporting the StealC and Amadey infrastructure on June 24, 2026. The post provides a technical overview of the StealC and Amadey malware families and the cybercrime services used to deliver them.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files migration assistant
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files migration assistant is in preview and available generally, using SnapMirror for data migration to ANF. It supports migrations from on-premises systems and from CVO or other cloud providers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds extended metadata for Replicate secrets
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning now adds extended metadata when it detects Replicate secrets, giving more context about leaked credentials. The change applies to the Replicate secret pattern and is meant to improve incident response and triage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Fetch Code Quality findings via REST API
item.description:
GitHub has added repository-level REST APIs for Code Quality findings in public preview. The new read-only endpoints expose code quality data via API, bringing parity closer to the GitHub UI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automatic Dependabot access to GitHub-hosted registries
item.description:
Dependabot can now read from private GitHub Packages registries without a personal access token when the package has granted repository access through “Manage Actions access.” This removes the need to configure a PAT for that dependency source.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot CLI: New terminal interface is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI’s redesigned terminal interface is now generally available. It adds a tabbed layout for working with GitHub directly from the terminal.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Deprecation of Python 3.9 for Dependabot
item.description:
Dependabot no longer supports Python 3.9 because it has reached end of life. Continuing to use Python 3.9 may prevent Dependabot from creating pull requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Agent Skills - Towards Autonomous Development, Deployment, and Validation🔥
item.description:
The article is a short note titled “Agent Skills - Towards Autonomous Development, Deployment, and Validation” with the phrase “aka, don’t ask me until prod.” No substantive technical details are provided in the supplied content.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app support for BYOK
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports bring your own key (BYOK), allowing agent sessions to use customer-managed model providers. Supported providers include OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic, and more.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Guarding AI memory
item.description:
Microsoft Security Blog discusses risks to AI memory and outlines defenses against attacks that target what an AI system remembers. The post is a high-level security overview rather than a product release note.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: One intrusion, two cyberattackers: Uncovering parallel threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft describes a ransomware case where two threat actors operated in parallel during the same intrusion, using overlapping tactics and evasion methods. The report emphasizes that isolated telemetry can miss complex attacks when activity from multiple actors is blended together.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: New features and Claude as agent provider preview in JetBrains IDEs
item.description:
GitHub added support for organization and enterprise agents in JetBrains IDEs, along with Copilot CLI message queueing/steering and a new agent debug logs summary view. The update also previews Claude as an agent provider in JetBrains IDEs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Where the agent decides, and where the tools actually run
item.description:
The article frames a design question about where to place an agent’s decision-making logic in an application that already has a deterministic state machine, tool integrations, and CI/CD. It focuses on separating the “brain” (judgment) from the “hands” (tool execution) within a graph/state-based architecture.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: The durable asset is the loop you own. OpenEnv is its protocol.
item.description:
The article argues that the durable asset in agentic AI is the learning loop, not the rented model, and presents OpenEnv as the protocol for reinforcement learning environments. It positions OpenEnv around owning and standardizing the environment/evaluation loop for recursive self-improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: AI credits consumed per user now in the Copilot usage metrics API
item.description:
The Copilot usage metrics API now includes per-user AI credits consumed per day. The new data is derived from the same AI credits consumption source used by the usage-based billing API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: AutoJack: How a single page can RCE the host running your AI agent
item.description:
Microsoft describes AutoJack, an exploit chain where a single malicious webpage can cause remote code execution on the host running an AI browsing agent. The attack abuses localhost trust, missing authentication, and unsafe parameter handling in AutoGen Studio’s MCP WebSocket.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of Opus 4.6 (fast)
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate Opus 4.6 (fast) across all Copilot experiences on June 29, 2026. This includes Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Outcome-driven learning systems: Enterprise RL with OpenEnv and Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft says its Build 2026 Foundry releases fit together as an outcome-driven learning system for enterprise reinforcement learning, centered on OpenEnv and Foundry. The post positions hosted agents, Toolboxes, Foundry IQ, Memory, Managed Compute, fine-tuning, Frontier Tuning, and a new evaluation/optimization stack as supporting pieces of that system.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1-Flash available on more Copilot surfaces
item.description:
MAI-Code-1-Flash is now available in additional GitHub Copilot surfaces. The model can be used in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot Chat on GitHub, and Visual Studio Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: New Forrester study shows customers who unified with Microsoft Security benefited from 124% ROI
item.description:
Microsoft cites a new Forrester Total Economic Impact study saying organizations that consolidated on Microsoft Security saw a 124% ROI, lower risk, and improved readiness to secure AI. The post is a summary announcement and does not include detailed methodology or product changes.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Copilot code review: AGENTS.md support and UI improvements
item.description:
Copilot code review now reads repository-level AGENTS.md files and adds a Request button to make it easier to ask Copilot for a review on draft pull requests. GitHub says these updates are generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Detecting Duplicate Issues – Public Preview and issue fields MCP support for GitHub Issues
item.description:
GitHub Issues adds duplicate issue detection in public preview and expands MCP support for issue fields. The change is aimed at reducing duplicate triage work for maintainers, especially in large repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot-authored pull requests now included in author searches
item.description:
Pull request searches using the author: qualifier now include pull requests opened by the Copilot cloud agent on a user’s behalf. For example, author:@me on GitHub pull requests will return those Copilot-authored PRs as well.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository switcher generally available in global navigation
item.description:
GitHub’s repository switcher in global navigation is now generally available. It lets you jump between repositories without leaving the current page.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions: Build custom images from custom images
item.description:
GitHub Actions custom images now support building one custom image from another. This adds flexibility for composing and managing image-generation pipelines for GitHub-hosted runners.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Safer pull_request_target defaults for GitHub Actions checkout
item.description:
GitHub is changing the default behavior of the Actions checkout action for workflows triggered by pull_request_target to reduce common security mistakes. The goal is to avoid exposing base-branch credentials or secrets to untrusted pull request code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Control who and what triggers GitHub Actions workflows
item.description:
GitHub Actions now has workflow execution protections in public preview for GitHub Enterprise, organizations, and repositories. Administrators can define allow lists to control which users or events can trigger workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Generated release notes credit you for Copilot pull requests
item.description:
Generated release notes now credit Copilot pull requests in the list of merged pull requests since the last release. This affects the automatically generated release notes output.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: From package to postinstall payload: Inside the Mastra npm supply chain compromise
item.description:
Microsoft describes a compromised npm package in the Mastra ecosystem that spread a hidden postinstall payload to 140+ projects. The post focuses on detection, hunting, and defense guidance using Microsoft Defender and threat intelligence.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Crypto Clipper uses Tor and worm-like propagation for persistence and control
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence described a cryptocurrency clipper campaign that steals and replaces wallet addresses, uses Tor for command-and-control, and spreads in a worm-like way. The malware also maintains persistence and includes a lightweight backdoor for follow-on activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Read remote repository content with GitHub CLI
item.description:
GitHub CLI now includes two commands for reading repository content without cloning: gh repo read-file and gh repo read-dir. These let you inspect remote files and directories directly from the terminal.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Beyond the benchmark: Advancing security at AI speed
item.description:
Microsoft Security says it has advanced its agentic vulnerability detection system, MDASH, and integrated it into workflows across Windows, Azure, and identity systems. The post focuses on applying the system in real-world security operations rather than benchmark results.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Secret scanning updates – June 2026
item.description:
GitHub added secret scanning coverage in June 2026 with new partner integrations, more default push-protection blocks, additional validity checks, and richer metadata for leaked secrets.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​Forrester names Microsoft a Leader in the 2026 Extended Detection and Response Platforms Wave™ report
item.description:
Microsoft says Forrester named it a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Extended Detection and Response Platforms, Q2 2026. The post is an announcement of the analyst recognition and does not include product changes or technical updates.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Databricks natively storing data in Microsoft OneLake
item.description:
Azure Databricks now supports natively writing managed Delta tables to Microsoft OneLake in public preview. This lets customers use OneLake as the storage layer for Databricks workloads without managing separate storage accounts.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Migrate – GitHub Copilot Modernization integration for at scale code assessments
item.description:
Azure Migrate public preview now integrates with GitHub Copilot Modernization to provide at-scale code insights. The integration combines Azure Migrate’s portfolio-level discovery and assessment with Copilot’s context-aware code analysis.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Databricks native read access to Microsoft OneLake
item.description:
Azure Databricks now has generally available native read access to Microsoft OneLake through Unity Catalog. Users can query and analyze OneLake data directly without moving or copying it.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support bypass permission controls
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now set disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" in enterprise-managed settings.json to prevent GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code from bypassing permission controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: AI-Powered MSBuild Investigation with the Microsoft Binlog MCP Server
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Binlog MCP Server for investigating MSBuild build failures and performance issues with AI. It provides 15 specialized tools for analyzing MSBuild binary logs through an AI assistant.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: AI is accelerating cyberattacks—here’s how to stay ahead
item.description:
Microsoft describes how its identity and security products use unified signals to help teams prevent, detect, and respond to AI-accelerated attacks faster. The post is a security-focused overview rather than a feature release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: ICMP Support for Azure Standard V2 NAT Gateway
item.description:
Azure StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports outbound ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply traffic. This lets customers use tools like ping to validate outbound connectivity and troubleshoot network issues from workloads behind the gateway.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Auto mode in Copilot Chat available for all users
item.description:
GitHub Copilot auto model selection is now generally available in Copilot Chat on github.com and the GitHub mobile app for all Copilot plans. In auto mode, Copilot selects the model for the chat request.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Limit open pull requests for users without write access
item.description:
GitHub is adding a limit on how many open pull requests users without write access can have in a repository. The change is intended to reduce repeated low-quality or drive-by PRs and ease triage load for maintainers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agent finder for GitHub Copilot now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes agent finder, a feature for selecting which MCP servers, skills, canvases, agents, and tools an agent should use. GitHub says it reduces the need to manually wire these components and helps avoid filling the context window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Introducing the Agentic Resource Discovery specification
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification, an open standard for AI clients to automatically find resources relevant to a task. It was developed with partners including GoDaddy, Google, and Hugging Face.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Copilot individual plan sign-ups are reopening
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Individual plans, including Student, Pro, Pro+, and Max, for new subscribers over the next couple of weeks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app is now generally available on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It serves as a native desktop app for agent-driven development on GitHub.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Models is no longer available to new customers
item.description:
GitHub is retiring GitHub Models. As an initial step, new customers can no longer use it, while existing organizations or enterprises that have already used it are not affected by this announcement.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: New project templates and template gallery for Azure Functions in VS Code
item.description:
The Azure Functions VS Code extension adds a redesigned Create New Project experience in public preview. It replaces the multi-step Quick Pick wizard with a searchable, filterable visual template gallery.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Log Analytics Summary Rules experience
item.description:
A new Azure portal experience for Summary Rules in Log Analytics is now generally available. Summary Rules aggregate high-volume log data on a defined schedule and store it in summarized tables for faster querying and reporting.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality generally available July 20, 2026
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality, currently in public preview, will reach general availability on July 20, 2026. The preview has been used by enterprises to detect maintainability and reliability issues, enforce quality gates, and track code coverage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Organization-level enablement for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality can now be enabled or disabled at the organization level with one toggle. This replaces the need to configure the feature repository by repository.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Information-flow control: Moving toward secure, autonomous agents
item.description:
The article says information-flow control (IFC) is a deterministic security approach that could help make autonomous agents more secure. It presents IFC as a path toward controlling how information moves through agent systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Copilot usage metrics now include more of your active users
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics now use server-side telemetry in addition to client-side signals, so reports include more active users. The change affects enterprise usage reports and improves coverage of user activity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Microsoft Defender email security benchmarking: Key insights from one year of data
item.description:
Microsoft published a blog post summarizing one year of real-world email security benchmarking for Microsoft Defender, comparing its performance against SEG and ICES vendors. The provided excerpt does not include the specific results or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on SIG Storage
item.description:
SIG Storage discusses its role in Kubernetes persistent storage, including CSI/COSI, data protection, and emerging work for AI workloads. Recent updates include VolumeGroupSnapshot GA in v1.36, CSI Changed Block Tracking Beta in v1.36, and VolumeAttributesClass GA in v1.34.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Copilot code review: New configurations and controls
item.description:
GitHub added new ways to configure Copilot code review, including organization runner controls, support for Copilot content exclusion, and removal of the repository custom instructions character limit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Minimum version enforcement timeline for self-hosted runners
item.description:
GitHub Actions is resuming enforcement of minimum version requirements for self-hosted runners on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency. The post says this is part of a broader effort to rebuild enforcement, but the excerpt does not include the specific minimum versions or timeline details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.21 is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.21 is now generally available. The release adds improvements in deployment efficiency, monitoring, code security, and policy management, including organization custom properties now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Bot-created pull requests can run workflows if approved
item.description:
Pull requests created by github-actions[bot] can now run CI/CD workflows after a user approves them. The approval step is required as a security check before generated code is allowed to trigger workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Av2-series, F-series, Fs-series, Fsv2-series, G-series, Gs-series, and Lsv2-series Virtual Machines for Azure Batch pools
item.description:
Azure Compute will retire several VM series used by Azure Batch pools on November 15, 2028. After that date, new Batch pools cannot use these series and existing pools must be moved to supported VM types.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: D-series, Ds-series, Dv2-series, Dsv2-series, and Ls-series Virtual Machines for Azure Batch pools
item.description:
Azure Compute will retire D-series, Ds-series, Dv2-series, Dsv2-series, and Ls-series VMs for Azure Batch pools on May 1, 2028. After that date, new Batch pools cannot be created with these VM series.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: GPv1 and Legacy Blob storage account creation
item.description:
Azure is retiring all General purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts, including legacy blob storage accounts. The notice says this is part of ongoing Azure Storage portfolio changes aimed at improving performance, scalability, and cost efficiency.

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL MCP Server
